result.rule: Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

result.rule: When the description says that reaching a deadline can determine which continuation occurs, while other outcomes may also occur first: Model the wait for the deadline as a timer intermediate catch event, using an event-based gateway when the deadline competes with other catching outcomes.

When the description makes completion contingent on both a time-based condition and a separate required activity, without stating that one must precede the other.: Model the time-based wait with an intermediate catch event and the activity as a parallel branch; synchronize the branches with a parallel gateway before completion.

When the description states that a report or message from an external participant conditionally triggers a continuation within an already-running process: Model receipt of the report as an intermediate message catch event in the existing process, rather than as a task or a new start event.

When the description states that a participant may perform an optional activity after the main process outcome has been reached: Model that activity as an optional continuation of the same process, rather than as a new process initiated by the activity.

result.rule: When the description states that an internal process sends information or an item to an external participant, or receives information or an item from one: Model the external participant as a separate pool and represent the stated communications with message flows.
When the description states that an external request or inquiry starts the process: Model the trigger as a start event, followed by a distinct task for receiving or handling the request.

When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.

When the description states that a report or message from an external participant conditionally triggers a continuation within an already-running process: Model receipt of the report as an intermediate message catch event in the existing process, rather than as a task or a new start event.
